title: Bugatti Refurbs a One-Off Polished Aluminum Veyron

body_markdown:
Bugatti launched[its Programme Solitaire division](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/bugatti-programme-solitaire-one-off-coachbuilding-details/) in 2025 to build one- and few-off cars, but the company has always been open to taking requests from customers. It notably built a Veyron Grand Sport Vitesse with a body made from exposed polished aluminum over 10 years ago. This one-of-a-kind Bugatti Veyron is still around today, and it was recently refurbished, reconfigured, and certified by the factory.


Commissioned by a customer, the project required a tremendous amount of work to complete. Bugatti never envisioned the Veyron with an aluminum body; Most of the body panels and the monocoque are made with carbon fiber. The brand explains that building the aluminum-bodied Veyron required shipping big blocks of aluminum weighing up to 22 tons to its factory in Molsheim, France.


The end result was head-turning, to say the least. The one-off Veyron features a mirror-like finish that’s almost reminiscent of[the Audi ASF concept](https://www.hagerty.com/media/automotive-history/vorsprung-durch-technik-audi-five-ways/) presented in 1993 to preview the aluminum-intensive first-generation A8. The carbon-fiber engine cover adds a touch of contrast to the look, and the exterior styling is complemented by a Carmine Red interior with exposed carbon-fiber trim.

Power comes from a quad-turbocharged, 8.0-liter W-16 engine rated at about 1183 horsepower and 1106 pound-feet of torque. Those figures may not sound that impressive when you consider that[the upcoming V-16-powered Tourbillon](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/bugattis-next-chapter-the-tourbillon/) is rated at 1800 horsepower, but they were jaw-dropping in the early 2000s. For context,[the Lamborghini Murcièlago](https://www.hagerty.com/media/car-profiles/lamborghini-murcielago-retro-drive/) made 575 horsepower.


The aluminum-bodied Veyron was ordered in 2014 and delivered in 2015, so it was[one of the last examples built](https://www.hagerty.com/media/market-trends/hagerty-insider/20-years-of-bugatti-veyron-how-does-the-market-treat-the-hallmark-hypercar/) . Fast-forward to 2026, and it returned to Molsheim where it was refurbished and reconfigured by Bugatti. The brand tells us that the work involved removing the non-original parts that were installed over the past decade or so to bring the Veyron back to its original condition.


The refurbishment work was commissioned by a collector who recently bought this one-off Bugatti Veyron. It’s now living on the French Riviera, where it’s sure to attract attention even in a part of the world where seven-digit supercars are a dime a dozen.
